body: I can't reproduce the crash on macOS, might be platform specific or timing sensitive.

I can't reproduce the issue When using the WTP script, sometimes the game freezes while closing and sometimes I get the following GDScript error.

```
E 0:00:01:364   _task: Cannot call method 'lock' on a null value.
  <GDScript Source>repro-WorkerThreadPool.gd:19 @ _task()
  <Stack Trace> repro-WorkerThreadPool.gd:19 @ _task()
```

The freeze is not really a freeze, it's just the engine is stuck waiting for the task to complete, but the task is explicitly made to take an absurd amount of time to complete. 

I can reproduce the error using the Threads example, but only when running the engine through an external c++ debugger. The error and crash happen after the following warning is spammed:

```
WARNING: A Thread object is being destroyed without its completion having been realized.
Please call wait_to_finish() on it to ensure correct cleanup.
     at: Thread::~Thread (core\os\thread.cpp:107)
```

Please note the [docs for Thread](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_thread.html) say

```
Warning:

To ensure proper cleanup without crashes or deadlocks, when a Thread's reference count reaches zero and it is therefore destroyed, the following conditions must be met:

- It must not have any Mutex objects locked.

- It must not be waiting on any Semaphore objects.

- wait_to_finish() should have been called on it.
```

I tested and confirmed that the crash goes away completely if you wait for the threads before exiting. 

For your reference, the following code does not crash. 

```gdscript
extends Node
# the goal is to see how many 30us operations i can squeeze out of any amount of threads

const THREAD_COUNT := 10
var workers := []
var result_queue := []
var queue_mutex := Mutex.new()
var finished_bool = false

func _ready():
	for i in THREAD_COUNT:
		var t := Thread.new()
		workers.append(t)
		t.start(_worker_loop.bind(i))

func _exit_tree() -> void:
	queue_mutex.lock()
	finished_bool = true
	queue_mutex.unlock()
	for i in THREAD_COUNT:
		workers[i].wait_to_finish()

func _worker_loop(_i):
	var result:bool
	while true:
		result = _task(0)
		queue_mutex.lock()
		if finished_bool == true:
			queue_mutex.unlock()
			return
		result_queue.append(result)
		queue_mutex.unlock()

 ## reports how many times the operation was run in the last [counter_max] frames
func _process(_delta):
	queue_mutex.lock()
	print(result_queue.size())
	result_queue.clear()
	queue_mutex.unlock()


func _task(_i: int) -> bool:
	wait_us(30)
	return true

func wait_us(us:int):
	var end_time:int = Time.get_ticks_usec() + us
	while Time.get_ticks_usec() < end_time:
		pass
```
